=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py:815-877 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_promote_cycle_runner_wait_retry_step_is_wired` is defined at line 877, after the `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard at line 873, and is not in main()'s explicit test list, so it never runs.
  WHY: CI runs this file as a script (`ci.yml:4332`, test-and-mark-stable.yml:3508, mark-stable.yml:597), so the poller retry-step wiring has no test that runs. Severities differed: BLOCKER (minimax), MAJOR (sonnet, gemini, glm), NIT (luna). The highest is used.
- tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_review_blocked_budget.py:1379-1441 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Five new Phase 4 runner-wait tests are defined after the `__main__` guard at line 1387, but main() at line 1379 collects tests from `globals()` before they exist. The tests are `test_phase4_runner_wait_stops_the_gate_when_enabled`, `test_phase4_runner_wait_does_not_stop_the_gate_by_default`, `test_phase4_runner_assigned_in_the_last_third_is_late_assigned`, `test_phase4_unconfirmed_long_empty_lookup_is_not_a_runner_wait` and `test_gate_workflow_enables_the_runner_wait_stop`.
  WHY: CI runs the file as a script (ci.yml:2874; test-and-mark-stable.yml:3442), so the gate-stop, default-off, late_assigned and empty-lookup tests never run, and main() still reports success. Severities differed: BLOCKER (minimax), MAJOR (sonnet, gemini, glm), NIT (luna). The highest is used.
- tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_dispatch_watch_timeout_cancel.py:379-390 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_gate_enables_the_runner_wait_stop_and_keeps_the_timeout_blocks` is defined at line 390, after the `__main__` guard at line 386 and after main() collects `globals()` at line 379, so it never runs.
  WHY: The `DISPATCH_WATCH_STOP_RELEASE_GATE` workflow-env contract, the `--stop-release-gate` default and the dispatch-step timeout blocks can all regress while CI reports `N passed`. Severities differed: BLOCKER (minimax), MAJOR (sonnet, gemini, glm). The highest is used.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:2027-2031 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The runner-wait allow-list `case "${failing_step}" in "Phase 4: Wait for review & autofix to complete"|"Dispatch & watch — "*)` does not match two watcher steps: "Dispatch internal-orchestrate.yml with multi-issue project" (test-and-mark-stable.yml:4129, watcher at 4169) and "Dispatch internal-validate.yml standalone" (test-and-mark-stable.yml:4539, watcher at 4556).
  WHY: A `RELEASE_GATE_RUNNER_WAIT outcome=stop_failed` from those jobs never reaches `HEAL_RUNNER_WAIT_MATCHED`. The check at lines 2116-2142 then sets `HEAL_RUNNER_WAIT_ALL=false` and a heal issue is filed, which violates G4. The agents.d fragment and the new tests have the same blind spot.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:2127-2138 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The runner-wait suppression applies only when `HEAL_RUNNER_WAIT_COUNT` is at most `MAX_FAILED_JOBS` (default 3, line 375).
  WHY: In a saturated queue, a gate with 4 or more failed runner-wait watch steps falls outside the suppression and files a heal issue, which starts more pipeline runs and defeats G4. Severities differed: NIT (sonnet), MAJOR (gemini, minimax, glm). The highest is used.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:2123 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The failed-job filter `select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "timed_out")` leaves out `startup_failure` jobs.
  WHY: A gate run with one `startup_failure` job plus runner-wait failures is skipped with `release_gate_runner_wait`, so a real defect never gets its heal issue.
- scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:1624-1705 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `promote_cycle_retry_check()` dispatches a full cycle (`gh workflow run ... -f cycle_retry=true`) without first calling `release_gate_oldest_queued_wait` to measure the current runner wait.
  WHY: While the queue stays long, each hourly retry takes a runner slot, skips again with `runner_wait_long` and re-arms the retry. That contradicts AD-1, G2 ("retried ... when the wait drops") and §26 until the AD-2 bound is reached.
- scripts/stable_e2e_step_wait_review.sh:383 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The `never_assigned` branch (`if [ -n "$REVIEW_RUNNER_WAIT_SINCE" ] && ... -le 2 ]; then rw_result_reason="never_assigned"`) has no minimum-duration or last-third check, unlike `late_assigned`.
  WHY: Suppose an earlier review run overran its budget and a replacement run was queued just before the deadline. The phase is classified `runner_wait=true`, the gate cancels itself, and a real overrun spends no attempt, which breaks the rule that G3 must not hide real failures.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:480-486 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `queued_no_runner` predicate counts jobs in `waiting`/`pending` status with no `runner_name` as runner waits, not only `status=queued` jobs.
  WHY: A child blocked on a concurrency group or a `needs:` dependency is classified `runner_wait`, and the gate is then cancelled when it should fail as a timeout, which hides real failures.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:477-487 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The runner-wait classification at line 486 requires all(...) jobs to be queued without a runner or to have started late.
  WHY: A watched run with one early successful job and another job still queued without a runner fails the `all(...)` test and is classified `timeout`, so the gate does not stop and the cycle is treated as failed.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:126-133 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The real-failure count `stop_real` in `dispatch_watch_stop_release_gate` (line 127) counts only `failure`/`timed_out` conclusions and leaves out `startup_failure`.
  WHY: A gate with a `startup_failure` job still cancels itself on a sibling's runner_wait and ends `cancelled`, which the release scripts read as no attempt used, so a real failure is hidden. auto_release_stable.sh:684/:487 treat `startup_failure` as a real failure.
- scripts/dispatch_and_watch_workflow_run.sh:545-551 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The "Stop the release gate on a runner wait" block cancels only the watched child (`WATCHED_RUN_ID`) and the gate. Children of the other dispatch steps keep running after the gate ends cancelled: validation-refresh, update_workflows, internal-memory-maintenance, internal-orchestrate, internal-validate standalone and the alt-model children.
  WHY: `dispatched_run_id`/`run_id` outputs are written only on completion (lines 386, 432), so the `if: always() && steps.<id>.outputs.run_id != ''` cleanups (e.g. line 3909) skip. This contradicts G3: "cancels the child runs it started".
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:16716 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The comprehensive-promotion outcome lookup `select(.event == "workflow_dispatch" and .created_at >= $since)] | sort_by(.created_at) | last` can match a poller cycle-retry run (`Promote main to stable [cycle-retry]`).
  WHY: A retry dispatched before the promotion run is listed becomes the newest match, so its result is read as the promotion's outcome. minimax and glm raised the same issue as a hardening suggestion only.
- scripts/auto_release_stable.sh:805 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The AD-2 bound takes the newest gate run from a fixed `per_page=30` listing (line 647). The same pattern is in scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh:1903 over `gate_runs_json` (`per_page=30`, line 1879).
  WHY: During a queue jam, newer runs push the newest stable or cycle gate run off the page. `rw_last_run_id` then points at a stale run, `bound_reached` fires, and the tick dispatches into the long wait. This fails open.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:4477-4512 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `release_gate_oldest_queued_wait` never checks that `_rgw_upper_epoch` is greater than `_rgw_lower`. If `RELEASE_GATE_MAX_RUNNER_WAIT_MINUTES` exceeds `ZOMBIE_RUN_MAX_QUEUED_HOURS*60`, the `created=` range is inverted.
  WHY: The API rejects the range (422) or returns nothing. Every tick then logs a generic `read_failed` and dispatches anyway, so the G1 check is silently off with no diagnostic.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
